destinations.name: Copper Coast
destinations.coordinates_source: candidate: Kadina (Wikipedia town point); recentre in pin step

name_evidence.wording: The Copper Coast: Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta (Moonta/Moonta Bay/Port Hughes was SA Top Tourism Town 2021); Wikivoyage covers Moonta and Wallaroo See listings

name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage "Yorke Peninsula and Clare Valley"; yorkepeninsula.com.au; visityorkepeninsula.com.au
name_evidence.wording: Yorke Peninsula, the peninsula-wide tourism name; this destination holds the east, centre and south coast outside the Copper Coast and Innes National Park

destinations.name: Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park
destinations.coordinates_source: candidate: Wikipedia area point (park centroid); needs the visitor point (visitor centre / campground)

name_evidence.wording: Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park, the headline Yorke attraction (Ethel wreck, lighthouses, surf, walks)

spots.bio: Cornish copper-mining site with the Hughes Pump House, Miners Cottage and a museum, where Australia's "Little Cornwall" began.
spots.name: Moonta Mines State Heritage Area
spots.note: 3 counted sources, 1729 page views

spots.bio: Sandy coves, beaches, a jetty and foreshore at the Moonta township, with Rossiters Point Lookout nearby.
spots.name: Moonta Bay
spots.note: Tourism board township page names sandy coves, beaches, jetty, foreshore and Rossiters Point Lookout (Moonta/Moonta Bay/Port Hughes was SA Top Tourism Town 2021); Wikivoyage Moonta covers the same coast. A beach-and-jetty stop of half an hour or more.

spots.bio: National Trust museum in Kadina with the stump-jump plough, Matta House and a miniature train.
spots.name: The Farm Shed Museum and Tourism Centre
spots.note: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage region page and yorkepeninsula.com.au (entry about $12) name this National Trust museum in Kadina with the stump-jump plough, Matta House and a miniature train; allow an hour or more.

spots.bio: Museum on Wallaroo's maritime and mining past, also running ghost tours.
spots.name: Wallaroo Heritage and Nautical Museum
spots.note: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Wallaroo See entry and yorkepeninsula.com.au; a museum open daily 10-4 with ghost tours.

spots.bio: Long swimming beach on the northern edge of Wallaroo, named by tourism sources.
spots.name: North Beach, Wallaroo
spots.note: Rule 1-2: both southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au name North Beach; a long swimming beach with a Wikipedia article.

spots.bio: Historic copper mine at Moonta with bookable underground tours through a 55 m tunnel.
spots.name: Wheal Hughes Copper Mine
spots.note: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Moonta and the YP region page both name the underground mine tour (55 m tunnel); a bookable, open visit of an hour or more.

spots.bio: Free water park at Moonta Bay, a permanent family venue worth an hour or two.
spots.name: Splash Town
spots.note: Rule 1-2: southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au both name this free water park at Moonta Bay, a permanent family venue worth an hour.

spots.bio: Seaside township and beach on the Copper Coast just south of Moonta Bay.
spots.name: Port Hughes
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 3446 page views

spots.bio: Sealed 25 km walking and cycling path along the old railway linking Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta.
spots.name: Copper Rail Trail
spots.note: 25 km sealed walking and cycling path between Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta, named by southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au attraction pages (rules 1, 2).

spots.bio: Red clay cliffs along the shore beside Ardrossan's historic jetty.
spots.name: Ardrossan Red Cliffs
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 5802 page views

spots.bio: Conservation park island with an 1855 cast-iron lighthouse and keeper's cottage, visited by boat from Edithburgh.
spots.name: Troubridge Island
spots.note: Rule 1/2: three counted sources including parks.sa.gov.au (Troubridge Island Conservation Park) and Wikivoyage Edithburgh: the 1855 cast-iron lighthouse and keepers cottage, visited by boat from Edithburgh (island is the spot, not the boat).

spots.bio: Tidal sea-water swimming pool set into the cliff at Edithburgh, with change rooms.
spots.name: Edithburgh Tidal Pool
spots.note: Rule 1/2: two counted sources (Wikivoyage Edithburgh Do and yorkepeninsula.com.au); a tidal sea-water swimming pool set into the cliff, with change rooms, free and always open.

spots.bio: Jetty known for diving and snorkelling among seahorses, Port Jackson sharks and leafy sea dragons.
spots.name: Edithburgh Jetty
spots.note: Wikivoyage lists it as its own destination (dive site), and the tourism board says it is renowned for diving and snorkelling with seahorses, Port Jackson sharks and leafy sea dragons; a jetty walk and shore dive a visitor goes for.

spots.bio: 1882 lighthouse reserve at the peninsula's south-western corner, reached by Lighthouse Road.
spots.name: Corny Point Lighthouse
spots.note: Listed as an attraction by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com; an 1882 lighthouse reserve reached by Lighthouse Road with a picnic area and coast to linger on; Wikivoyage names it too. Free, self-guided.

spots.bio: Salt lakes on the Yorke Peninsula Salt Lake Trail, with a viewing platform at Pink Lake and a boardwalk at Par Lake.
spots.name: Yorketown Pink Lakes
spots.note: Tourism board and southaustralia.com name the Yorke Peninsula Salt Lake Trail (self-drive routes, boardwalk at Par Lake, Pink Lake viewing platform, 15 to 90 min). Objection: lake colour varies by season, and it could duplicate a Salt Lake Trail candidate.

spots.bio: Old port jetty and cliff-top lime kilns with a lookout on the coast road.
spots.name: Wool Bay Jetty and Lime Kilns
spots.note: Tourism board page names the uniquely designed lime kilns on the cliff top and the old port jetty, with a lookout; a free heritage stop on the coast road. Objection: a short stop, one source.

spots.bio: Western-coast town with an 1878 jetty, a maritime museum and a geology trail.
spots.name: Port Victoria
spots.note: Town with a historic 1878 jetty, Port Victoria Maritime Museum and geology trail; named by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com (rules 1, 2).

spots.bio: 1877 cargo shed by the jetty telling the story of the windjammer grain races.
spots.name: Port Victoria Maritime Museum
spots.note: Two sources: yorkepeninsula.com.au Port Victoria page and visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (1877 cargo shed by the jetty telling the windjammer grain-race story). Objection: open weekends 2-4 pm only.

spots.bio: Free display of the Red Devil monoplane that made the first airmail flight over the sea.
spots.name: Minlaton Harry Butler Red Devil Memorial
spots.note: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Minlaton and the yorkepeninsula.com.au Minlaton page (the only genuine Red Devil monoplane, first airmail over the sea, free display on the edge of town).

spots.bio: Seaside town on the east coast of the Yorke Peninsula with a beach and jetty.
spots.name: Port Vincent
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 2594 page views

spots.bio: 1876 jetty still used by fishers and white beaches on Hardwicke Bay, with boating and diving.
spots.name: Point Turton
spots.note: Tourism board page: 1876 jetty (still used by fishers), white beaches on Hardwicke Bay, boating and diving; a second-tier seaside stop. Beach and jetty are one place (Point Turton Beach is a duplicate).

spots.bio: Surf breaks and three swimming beaches, with a coastal drive from Corny Point to Berry Bay.
spots.name: Corny Point
spots.note: Tourism board page names surf breaks (Rock Pool, Salmon Hole, Daly Head, Berry Bay), three swimming beaches and the Corny Point to Berry Bay coastal drive; visitors beaches stop. Lighthouse is a separate candidate.

spots.bio: Safe white-sand beach with no rips, good for crabbing and swimming, beside Pine Point.
spots.name: Black Point
spots.note: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage (own section with Pine Point, "one of the most gorgeous stretches of coastline") and the tourism board page (safe white-sand beach with no rips, crabbing, swimming).

spots.bio: White-sand swimming beach south of Edithburgh, at the end of the mosaic walking trail.
spots.name: Sultana Point
spots.note: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Edithburgh Do names it as the swimming beach south of town with white sand and the end of the mosaic walking trail; a second-tier beach stop (COVERAGE.md).

spots.bio: Museum in the old Smith stump-jump plough factory, with a Zanoni shipwreck display.
spots.name: Ardrossan Heritage Museum
spots.note: Two sources: yorkepeninsula.com.au and visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (in the old Smith stump-jump plough factory, shipwreck Zanoni display, open seven days 10-4).

spots.bio: 1878 schoolroom in Stansbury holding farm and industry displays, open only some afternoons.
spots.name: Stansbury Museum
spots.note: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Stansbury See; visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page): 1878 schoolroom with farm and industry displays. Objection: volunteer-run, open Wed and Sun afternoons.

spots.bio: Museum in a former produce store covering the salt industry and shipwrecks, open at weekends.
spots.name: Edithburgh Museum
spots.note: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Edithburgh See (adults $3) and the visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (salt industry, shipwrecks, produce-store building). Objection: weekend afternoons only.

spots.bio: Private museum with a large WWI, WWII and Vietnam collection and memorial gardens.
spots.name: Bublacowie Military Museum
spots.note: Two sources: visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (extensive WWI/WWII/Vietnam collection, memorial gardens, tours) and History SA; guided visits last an hour or two. Objection: private museum, open Sun to Tue or by appointment.

spots.bio: Lighthouse and lookout on Cape Spencer, also the park's whale-watching cliff.
spots.name: Cape Spencer Lighthouse
spots.note: Lighthouse and lookout on Cape Spencer in Innes National Park, named by parks.sa.gov.au and yorkepeninsula.com.au (Cape Spencer Lookout); also the park's whale-watching cliff. One spot with Cape Spencer (duplicate).

spots.bio: Surf beach and campground at the western end of the park.
spots.name: Pondalowie Bay
spots.note: Surf beach and campground in the park, named by parks.sa.gov.au and yorkepeninsula.com.au; a beach (and Yorke's best-known surf break) is a standard second-tier keep.

spots.bio: Remains of the 1904 wreck of the Ethel on Ethel Beach.
spots.name: Ethel Wreck
spots.note: Remains of the Ethel (1904) on Ethel Beach in the park, named by parks.sa.gov.au ('Visit... the shipwreck of the Ethel') and yorkepeninsula.com.au (rules 1, 2). Ethel Beach is a duplicate of this.

spots.bio: Headland lookout reached by a 4 km return walk with views of the rugged coast.
spots.name: Royston Head
spots.note: Headland lookout, 2-hour 4 km return hike with 'amazing views of the rugged peninsula coast' (parks.sa.gov.au); a headland a guide singles out, second tier but real.

spots.bio: Village in the park with the visitor centre, jetty and campground.
spots.name: Stenhouse Bay
spots.note: Village in Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park with the visitor centre, jetty, campground and whale-watching cliffs; named by yorkepeninsula.com.au and the parks page (rules 1, 2). Stands in for Stenhouse Bay Jetty (duplicate).

spots.bio: 1 km loop to West Cape lighthouse with 360 degree views.
spots.name: West Cape Headland Hike
spots.note: 30-minute 1 km loop to West Cape lighthouse with 360 degree views, named on parks.sa.gov.au and highlighted by rangers (rules 1, 2).

spots.bio: Abandoned gypsum township with ruins, interpretive signs and heritage cottages.
spots.name: Inneston
spots.note: Abandoned gypsum township in the park, a named see on the parks.sa.gov.au page (ruins, interpretive signs, heritage cottages); one spot with Inneston Historic Walk (duplicate of this).

spots.bio: 2 km cliff-top loop with views over Investigator Strait.
spots.name: Stenhouse Bay Lookout Walk
spots.note: parks.sa.gov.au lists it as an easy 1 hour, 2 km cliff-top loop with views over Investigator Strait "among the best in the park"; a distinct walk from the jetty car park.

spots.bio: Beach in Innes National Park on the road to Royston Head, named as one to visit in the park.
spots.name: Dolphin Beach
spots.note: Named as a beach to visit in Innes National Park by the Tourism Australia G'day Parks guide (and photographed by southaustralia.com); sits on the Royston Head road. Objection: parks.sa.gov.au gives it only a passing mention, so a single guide source.

spots.bio: Seaside village at the entrance to Innes National Park, with a beach and the park gate.
spots.name: Marion Bay
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 3151 page views

spots.bio: 9.8 km hike through dunes and mallee between Browns Beach and Gym Beach, the longest trail in the park.
spots.name: Gym Beach Hike
spots.note: Agency-listed 4 hour, 9.8 km hike through dunes and mallee between Browns Beach and Gym Beach; Wikivoyage calls it the longest trail in the park.

spots.bio: 7.6 km hike along the old railway from Inneston to Stenhouse Bay, with interpretive signs.
spots.name: Thomson-Pfitzner Plaster Trail
spots.note: Agency-listed 3 hour, 7.6 km hike along the old railway from Inneston to Stenhouse Bay with interpretive signs; Wikivoyage lists it too (though calls it the least interesting trail). Objection: overlaps the Inneston ruins, a plain track.

spots.bio: Northern Yorke Peninsula town with a jetty and a shoreline on the Spencer Gulf estuary.
spots.name: Port Broughton
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 6461 page views

spots.bio: Local heritage museum in Port Broughton, open only on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.
spots.name: Port Broughton Heritage Centre and Museum
spots.note: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Port Broughton, $7 entry; yorkepeninsula.com.au Port Broughton page); a permanent venue, small hours do not make it an event. Objection: open only Tue and Thu 1-3 pm.

spots.bio: Gateway town where the road onto the Yorke Peninsula leaves the Adelaide Plains.
spots.name: Port Wakefield
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 6009 page views

spots.bio: About 500 km of coastal walking trail around the Yorke Peninsula, in sections.
spots.name: Walk the Yorke
spots.note: 3 counted sources, 0 page views

spots.bio: Heritage trail of interpretive signs at wreck sites around the southern coast from Edithburgh to Innes.
spots.name: Investigator Strait Shipwreck Trail
spots.note: Heritage trail named by the SA government, southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au (interpretive signs around the southern coast from Edithburgh to Innes, including the Ethel wreck). Objection: mainly a dive trail, spread over many sites.

review.name: Kernewek Lowender
review.reason: 3 counted sources and 1794 views but a biennial Cornish festival is an event, not a permanent place (COVERAGE.md rule 4); mention in the Copper Coast description and best-time text, no spot

merged.reason: town is a wrapper for its attraction; mention in Copper Coast description

merged.reason: same beach and foreshore; judge notes both cover the Moonta Bay coast

merged.reason: same point and same cliffs and jetty; town wrapper

merged.reason: town wrapper for its museum; mention in description

merged.name: Edithburgh

merged.reason: town wrapper beside four of its own attractions

merged.into: Minlaton Harry Butler Red Devil Memorial

merged.reason: the park is the destination, not a spot of itself
